arguments.text: Strong start. Settle now, find your long race rhythm.

Plan (min 1): 10 km, 10 legs of 1000 m. Start 27-30 pct above CP (boat 154 vs 118 W, pod 212 vs 167 W). Cued ease to 158 s/500 ground at min 1. Target: settle near CP (boat ~118-122 W, pod ~167-172 W), even effort, check reserve trends, sprint last ~600-800 m. push_local 0.23 on leg 1 heading north with push_along 0.03: check after turn whether it flips (current) or stays (model bias).

arguments.message: GPS speed well below what pod power should give: rudder snag, drag, or adverse current. Compare with leg direction.
Pod reserve below 35 pct with more than 1.2 km left.

arguments.condition: shaft_power_w > sustainable_shaft_power_w * 1.08 and elapsed_s > 240 and remaining_m > 1200
arguments.message: Shaft power more than 8 pct above sustainable for 90 s.

arguments.condition: shaft_power_w < cp_shaft_w * 0.9 and elapsed_s > 240 and remaining_m > 1200
arguments.message: Shaft power more than 10 pct below pod CP for 2 min: leaving time on the water or tiring.
Final km: plan the finishing sprint.

text: Cued ease to 158 s/500 after a start 27-30 pct above CP; noted plan; set watches for drag/current, low reserve, over/under pacing and the final km.

arguments.text: Still too hot. Ease off, settle at 159 pace.

Min 4: still 11-14 pct above CP (boat 131 W, pod 190 W), reserve boat 37 pct / pod 47 pct, display pace 152.7 vs my 158 target. Cued ease to 159 at min 4. Paddler says 6/10 hard but holding: either CP is underestimated or they misjudge. Check: if power settles near CP and reserve still falls, CP too high; if reserve flat and they feel fine above CP, CP may be low. push_along +0.07 on leg 1 (north).

text: Cued ease to 159: still 11-14 pct above CP with reserve near 40 pct after 4 min; paddler reports 6/10.

arguments.text: Ease a touch more. Smooth and long, 162 pace this leg.

Min 6.2 (leg 2, south, push -0.04): pod 180 W (+7.6 pct over CP), boat 130 W, reserve pod 34 / boat 23 pct, fade -0.8 (none). Cued ease to 162 ground. Pace targets are OVER GROUND: north legs (odd) have ~+0.05 push, south legs (even) ~-0.04, so target ~158 north / ~162 south for sustainable. Paddler follows pace targets fairly well. CP test idea: if reserve model reads under 10 pct but fade stays above -1 and paddler feels ok, raise CP (set_critical_power).

text: Cued ease to 162 ground pace: still 8-10 pct above CP with pod reserve at 34 pct; no fade yet.

arguments.text: Min 9.2: settled. Boat 119 W (at CP), pod 174 W (+4 pct, sustainable 168.5), reserve pod 22 / boat 12 pct, display 161.3 vs target 162. Paddler 7/10 hard but holding. fade_pct -3.4 is mostly my easing at the same rate (64 spm), not fatigue: shaft/boat power ratio steady ~0.69. No cue: on plan. If pod stays above ~170 for long, reserve empties around km 3.5: a gentle hold cue may be needed.

text: No cue: settled near sustainable pace (boat at CP, pod 4 pct over), paddler 7/10 and following the 162 target.

arguments.text: Creeping up again. Ease slightly, steady 159 pace this leg.

arguments.message: Pod shaft power more than 4.5 pct above sustainable for 2 min: paddler drifting up again.
Shaft power fell more than 14 pct below CP for 30 s: possible blow-up, rudder problem or loss of focus.
Pod reserve model empty but paddler still above pod CP for 3 min: CP probably underestimated.

arguments.text: Min 12.2 (leg 3 north): paddler drifts back to pod ~177 W (CP 167, sustainable 168) whenever a cue fades; reserve pod 14 / boat 3 pct. Paddler 7/10 steady at min 4, 9, 12. TRUST POD reserve: boat power jumps on north legs (helping current that push_along underestimates; push_local +0.05 north, ~-0.02 south), so boat reserve over-drains. Cued ease to 159 ground at min 12.2. Watches: over_sustainable2 (pod > 1.045x sustainable 2 min), blowup, cp_too_low (pod reserve empty but holding above CP 3 min -> raise cp_shaft).

text: Cued ease to 159 ground: paddler drifted back to 6 pct over pod CP with pod reserve at 14 pct; added drift, blow-up and CP-too-low watches.
No cue: pod power 169 W is at sustainable, paddler on the 159 target; pod reserve 8 pct, watches cover drift and blow-up.

arguments.text: Back off a little. Smooth strokes, 163 pace this leg.

Min 18.2 (leg 4 south): pod 180 W again, pod reserve model 0, no fade yet (-1.7). Paddler effort climbing 6,7,7,8 (8/10 at min 18). Cued ease to 163 ground (south). If no blow-up and effort steady at ~175 W over next 5-10 min, raise cp_shaft to ~173.

text: Cued ease to 163 ground: paddler back at 8 pct over pod CP with model reserve empty and effort rising to 8/10.
No cue: this drift alert is the one my ease-to-163 cue a few seconds ago already answers; it needs 10-20 s to act.

arguments.reason: Pod reserve model has read empty for 3 min while the paddler held 173-180 W shaft with no loss of speed at the same power; about 16.6 kJ spent above 167 W vs a 14.3 kJ test reserve, so CP or reserve is underestimated. Modest +3 pct raise.

arguments.text: Min 19.8: cp_too_low fired (pod reserve 0 for 3 min at 173-180 W, no efficiency fade; speed drop matches power drop). Raised cp_shaft 167->172, boat CP 118->121. Paddler now 172.6 after my 163 cue. Plan: hold ~172-175 shaft; if cp_too_low fires again (above 175 with empty reserve 3 min, no fade), raise to ~176. If blowup fires, ease hard and lower CP back.

text: No cue: paddler already eased to 172 W after my last cue; raised CP to 172 W shaft / 121 W boat on evidence of holding above it with an empty reserve and no fade.
No cue: shaft 171 W holds right at the revised CP of 172 W, pace steady at 159 on the north leg, no fade beyond the power change.

arguments.text: Min 25.8 (halfway): paddler drifts 170-180 W shaft, avg ~175 over 20 min, no blow-up, effort 8/10 steady since min 18. Excess above 167 W now ~19 kJ (> test reserve +25 pct), so true CP likely 172-178. No cue: saving cues for finish. Finish plan: build from ~800 m out, finish cue at ~600 m.

text: No cue: paddler at 179 W, a little above revised CP, but effort steady 8/10 for 8 min and no fade; evidence says true CP is 172-178 W.

arguments.text: Headwind now. Slower pace is fine, hold this effort.

Min 27.8: radio says south wind 8-12 kn filling in. South legs (even: 6, 8, 10 incl the finish) are now INTO the wind (push_local -0.14), north legs (7, 9) downwind. Boat-speed numbers (power_w, reserve_left_pct, sustainable pace, fade) now read the wind as the paddler: use pod only. Plan: hold ~178-180 shaft into the wind, ease to ~168-170 on downwind legs; cued hold at 180 W on leg 6.

text: Cued hold: south wind on the south leg, so keep the 180 W effort into the wind and accept a slower display pace; ease on downwind legs later.

arguments.reason: Second time the pod reserve read empty for 3 min with the paddler at 177-180 W and no blow-up; effort report steady at 8/10. Average about 175-177 W over 25 min with nothing in reserve. Raise to 176 W shaft.

arguments.message: Now heading north = downwind leg: cue a slight ease (about 170-172 W shaft).

arguments.text: Min 29.8: cp_too_low fired again (180 W, pod reserve 0, 3 min). Raised cp_shaft 172->176, boat 121->124. Headwind leg 6 push_local -0.22, display 170, paddler holding 180 as cued. Watch downwind_leg wakes me after each north turn to cue a slight ease; back to hold ~180 on south legs.

text: No cue: holding 180 W into the headwind is what I want; raised CP to 176 W shaft after a second empty-reserve stretch with no blow-up; watch set for the downwind turn.

arguments.text: Tailwind leg now. Ease a touch, ride the runs, save it.

arguments.message: Now heading south = into the wind: cue hold/push to about 180 W shaft.

text: Cued a slight ease on the downwind leg (push flipping positive confirms wind, not a rudder snag) to spend more effort into the wind; watch set for the next upwind turn.

arguments.message: Recheck: paddler reported a heavy boat / something on the rudder at min 32.4. Compare push_local on this downwind leg (expect about +0.15 to +0.2) and decide on clear_rudder.
On a downwind leg the boat is slower than pod power should give: likely weed on the rudder.

arguments.text: Min 32.4: paddler said legs are going, close to the limit, and boat feels heavy, something on the rudder? At that moment push_local was still rising after the north turn (+0.16, tailwind), no drop seen yet. Cued ease at 32.3. True CP probably ~172-175, not 176+: ease on downwind leg 7, hold ~175 (not 180) into wind on leg 8. If push_local on north leg falls toward 0 or below, cue clear_rudder.

text: No cue yet (gate closed for under a minute; ease cue just given): set watches to recheck the possible rudder snag shortly and to flag a downwind slowdown.

arguments.text: Rudder reads clear. Ease a little more, recover on this tailwind.

Min 33.4: no snag: downwind push_local +0.18 (headwind leg was -0.21), fade -1.5 = normal. Did NOT clear rudder. Cued ease again to let legs recover on leg 7 (paddler near limit). Plan: leg 8 into wind hold ~175, leg 9 ease ~170, leg 10 into wind finish from ~600 m.

text: Cued ease with reassurance that the rudder reads clear (downwind push +0.18 as expected, no drag sign); paddler near the limit, so recover on the tailwind.

arguments.reason: Paddler went from 8/10 to legs going at min 32 and 10/10 at min 36 after 6 min at 178-182 W. Reserve spent above 172 W totals about 15 kJ, close to the test reserve, so CP near 172 W shaft fits best; 176 was too high.

arguments.text: Min 36.4: paddler 10/10 close to limit at 171 W shaft. Best fit: true CP ~172 W shaft with reserve ~15 kJ, now about empty (ran out ~min 31). Set CP back to 172/121. Rest of race: hold 168-171 on leg 8 (into wind), ~165-168 on leg 9 (downwind) to rebuild a little, then leg 10 into wind: hold, then finish sprint only in the last ~400-500 m. Do not push into the wind early.

arguments.message: Now heading south = into the wind. Paddler near limit: cue hold at about 170 W shaft (CP 172), do NOT push until the final 400-500 m.

text: No cue: paddler at 10/10 holding 171 W, just under the corrected 172 W CP; lowered CP back to 172 and set the upwind-turn watch to cue a steady hold, not a push.

arguments.text: Breathe, settle, keep the rhythm. Power will come back.

arguments.message: Paddler has recovered above 160 W after the blow-up at min 36.5: cue a steady hold around 165-170 W, no surges until the last 400 m.

arguments.text: Min 37.1: BLOW-UP at 2.0 km left... correction 3.0 km left: shaft fell 181 -> 137 W over 60 s right after the turn into the wind (leg 8), paddler 8/10 close to limit. True reserve was spent by the 178-181 W surges. Cued reassure (no push). Watch recovered wakes me when back above 160 W. Finish sprint only in the last ~300-400 m, and only if power has recovered.

text: Cued reassure after a blow-up (shaft 181 to 137 W, paddler at limit); no push, and a watch to wake me when power recovers above 160 W.
No cue: gate closed and the reassure cue for the blow-up is still acting; push_local -0.35 includes the turn, the drag watch will flag it if it stays that low.

arguments.message: Cue gate open again and push_local still very low on leg 8: cue clear_rudder (paddler asked about the rudder at min 32.4; leg 8 push -0.32 vs -0.21 on leg 6 into the same wind).

arguments.text: Min 37.8: drag alarm on leg 8 into wind: push_local -0.32 vs -0.21 on leg 6 (same wind, 180 W). Extra ~0.1 m/s could be wind building or weed on rudder (paddler asked at 32.4). Clearing costs a few s, a snag would cost ~30 s over 2.9 km: plan clear_rudder at min 38.3 when the gate opens; afterwards check whether push_local jumps by ~0.1.

text: No cue yet (gate opens in under 30 s): drag alarm on the upwind leg; set a watch to cue clear_rudder when the gate opens if the boat is still slow.
